person.name: Mike Grabowski
person.role: Senior React Native Engineer & OSS Lead

skills.name: React Native Core
evidence: PR #2847: Refactored the native modules bridge to support async initialization.
React Native EU 2024 talk on migrating 200+ modules to the new architecture.

skills.name: Build Systems & Tooling
evidence: Created Re.Pack, enabling code splitting and module federation in React Native.
Implemented tree-shaking for native modules in Re.Pack v3.
Explained custom Metro transformer architecture on a podcast.

skills.name: JavaScript Engine Integration
evidence: Wrote about integrating Hermes on iOS and profiling startup time.
Added Hermes bytecode precompilation to the CLI build step.

skills.name: Open Source Leadership
evidence: Managed 50+ contributors across React Native CLI and Re.Pack.
Regularly helped community members debug native module issues.
Mentored three junior engineers on OSS contribution workflows.

skills.name: Architecture Design
evidence: Talk on designing plugin architectures for React Native tooling.
Authored autolinking specification and configuration API docs.
Led modular architecture discussions for a monorepo migration.

skills.name: Native Modules (iOS/Android)
evidence: Authored the Turbo Modules migration guide.
Bridged a native camera module with new architecture support.

gapSummary: Mike's departure creates critical gaps in React Native build tooling ownership, JavaScript engine integration expertise, and open-source community leadership. The team loses its primary architecture decision-maker for cross-platform tooling and the main bridge between the React Native core team and the broader OSS community.

recommendedRole.title: Staff React Native Platform Engineer
recommendedRole.description: Own React Native build infrastructure, native module architecture, and developer tooling. Lead OSS community engagement around internal frameworks and drive architectural decisions for cross-platform tooling.

scorecard.description: Deep understanding of Fabric, TurboModules, and the JSI bridge. Can debug native crashes and performance issues at the engine level.
Experience with Metro, Webpack, or custom bundlers for mobile. Understands code splitting, tree-shaking, and bytecode compilation.
Track record maintaining popular OSS projects. Can manage community contributions, triage issues, and drive roadmap decisions publicly.
Comfortable writing and debugging native modules in Swift/ObjC and Kotlin/Java. Understands Gradle and CocoaPods.
Can design plugin systems, define API contracts, and make trade-offs for long-lived developer tools.
Writes clear technical docs, gives talks, and mentors junior engineers effectively.

interviewQuestions.question: Walk us through how you'd debug a React Native app that crashes on startup only on Android 12+ devices after enabling the new architecture.
You need to implement code splitting for a React Native app with 50+ feature modules. How would you approach it and what trade-offs would you evaluate?
Describe a time you made a controversial technical decision in an open-source project. How did you communicate it and handle pushback?
Design a native module for biometric authentication across iOS and Android. How would you handle platform differences?
An OSS contributor submits a large PR that refactors your plugin system and changes the public API. How do you handle it?
You're tasked with reducing JS bundle startup time by 40%. Where do you start and what metrics do you track?

mustHave: 3+ years hands-on React Native experience beyond web React.
Experience with native module development on iOS or Android.
Track record in build tooling or developer experience work.
Published OSS work or significant contributions to major projects.
Strong written and verbal technical communication.
niceToHave: Experience with Hermes or other JavaScript engines.
Knowledge of Module Federation or micro-frontend patterns.
Experience managing a team of 3+ engineers.
Rust or C++ for performance-critical native modules.
redFlags: Only web React experience with no native mobile background.
No open-source contributions or community involvement.
Cannot explain the build pipeline beyond npm scripts.
Dismissive of backward compatibility and migration paths.
No experience working asynchronously with distributed teams.
